question: On p1, investigate the cached SHOPAPP SELECT that reads PRICE from PRODUCTS by PRODUCT_ID, last active between 1 Oct 2026 and 1 Jan 2027 UTC (start included, end excluded). If several statement IDs match, choose the lexicographically lowest. Use existing evidence without executing the statement; if absent, report a cache miss. Report each plan hash value and the number of cached child cursors using it. Does the cache demonstrate multiple plans? Do not infer a historical regression from one cached plan.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT s.plan_hash_value AS plan_hash_value, COUNT(*) AS child_count FROM v$sql s WHERE s.sql_id=(SELECT s.sql_id FROM v$sql s WHERE s.parsing_schema_name='SHOPAPP' AND s.command_type=3 AND UPPER(s.sql_text) LIKE 'SELECT PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE PRODUCT_ID%' AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') >= TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2026-10-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') < TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2027-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') ORDER BY s.sql_id FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) GROUP BY s.plan_hash_value ORDER BY s.plan_hash_value

question: On p1, investigate the cached SHOPAPP SELECT that reads PRICE from PRODUCTS by PRODUCT_ID, last active between 1 Oct 2026 and 1 Jan 2027 UTC (start included, end excluded). If several statement IDs match, choose the lexicographically lowest. Use existing evidence without executing the statement; if absent, report a cache miss. Find the table and indexes referenced by its cached plan. For each, give the object name, whether optimizer statistics are stale, and the last analyzed timestamp in UTC, to the second. Distinguish missing statistics from fresh statistics.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t.owner AS owner, t.table_name AS object_name, NVL(t.stale_stats,'UNKNOWN') AS stale_stats, TO_CHAR(FROM_TZ(CAST(t.last_analyzed AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') AT TIME ZONE '+00:00','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') AS last_analyzed_utc FROM dba_tab_statistics t JOIN v$sql_plan p ON p.object_owner=t.owner AND p.object_name=t.table_name WHERE p.sql_id=(SELECT s.sql_id FROM v$sql s WHERE s.parsing_schema_name='SHOPAPP' AND s.command_type=3 AND UPPER(s.sql_text) LIKE 'SELECT PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE PRODUCT_ID%' AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') >= TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2026-10-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') < TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2027-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') ORDER BY s.sql_id FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) AND t.object_type='TABLE' UNION SELECT DISTINCT i.owner AS owner, i.index_name AS object_name, NVL(i.stale_stats,'UNKNOWN') AS stale_stats, TO_CHAR(FROM_TZ(CAST(i.last_analyzed AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') AT TIME ZONE '+00:00','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') AS last_analyzed_utc FROM dba_ind_statistics i JOIN v$sql_plan p ON p.object_owner=i.owner AND p.object_name=i.index_name WHERE p.sql_id=(SELECT s.sql_id FROM v$sql s WHERE s.parsing_schema_name='SHOPAPP' AND s.command_type=3 AND UPPER(s.sql_text) LIKE 'SELECT PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE PRODUCT_ID%' AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') >= TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2026-10-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') < TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2027-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') ORDER BY s.sql_id FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) AND i.object_type='INDEX' ORDER BY owner, object_name

question: On p1, investigate the cached SHOPAPP SELECT that reads PRICE from PRODUCTS by PRODUCT_ID, last active between 1 Oct 2026 and 1 Jan 2027 UTC (start included, end excluded). If several statement IDs match, choose the lexicographically lowest. Use existing evidence without executing the statement; if absent, report a cache miss. For the lowest numbered child, report each captured-bind metadata entry: bind name, position, datatype, and whether capture occurred. Do not retrieve or disclose bind values.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT b.name AS bind_name, b.position AS position, b.datatype_string AS datatype, b.was_captured AS was_captured FROM v$sql_bind_capture b WHERE (b.sql_id,b.child_number) IN (SELECT s.sql_id,s.child_number FROM v$sql s WHERE s.sql_id=(SELECT s.sql_id FROM v$sql s WHERE s.parsing_schema_name='SHOPAPP' AND s.command_type=3 AND UPPER(s.sql_text) LIKE 'SELECT PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE PRODUCT_ID%' AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') >= TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2026-10-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') < TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2027-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') ORDER BY s.sql_id FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) ORDER BY s.child_number FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) ORDER BY b.position

question: On p1, investigate the cached SHOPAPP SELECT that reads PRICE from PRODUCTS by PRODUCT_ID, last active between 1 Oct 2026 and 1 Jan 2027 UTC (start included, end excluded). If several statement IDs match, choose the lexicographically lowest. Use existing evidence without executing the statement; if absent, report a cache miss. Across its cached children, how many distinct non-null SQL plan baseline names and SQL profile names are attached? Explain whether zero attached names proves that no matching management objects exist anywhere.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT s.sql_id AS sql_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.sql_plan_baseline) AS attached_baseline_count, COUNT(DISTINCT s.sql_profile) AS attached_profile_count FROM v$sql s WHERE s.sql_id=(SELECT s.sql_id FROM v$sql s WHERE s.parsing_schema_name='SHOPAPP' AND s.command_type=3 AND UPPER(s.sql_text) LIKE 'SELECT PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE PRODUCT_ID%' AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') >= TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2026-10-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') AND FROM_TZ(CAST(s.last_active_time AS TIMESTAMP), '+00:00') < TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ('2027-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS TZH:TZM') ORDER BY s.sql_id FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY) GROUP BY s.sql_id
